territorial_scope.description: Amends the New York State Election Law and applies to political communications in elections under that law.

evidence.quote: the supreme court where the materially deceptive media at issue could deceive and influence electors in an upcoming election

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends New York Election Law § 14-106 so that persons who distribute political communications containing materially deceptive media, with actual knowledge of that, must disclose it using a prescribed label, subject to exemptions. Candidates depicted without consent may seek injunctive relief and costs. Takes effect immediately.
summary.long: Amends Election Law § 14-106 to require disclosure when a person, campaign, committee or organization distributes a political communication containing materially deceptive media that it knows to be materially deceptive. Visual media must carry the statement 'This (image, video, or audio) has been manipulated' in a font no smaller than other text; audio must state it at the start and end and, if longer than two minutes, at intervals of no more than two minutes. Exemptions cover satire or parody, news reporting that acknowledges questions about authenticity, paid broadcasts by stations with consistent disclaimer requirements, and initial dissemination by platforms of content from other providers. A candidate whose voice or likeness appears without consent may seek injunctive relief, court costs and attorneys' fees in the supreme court, with expedited proceedings. Preliminary relief is available where plaintiffs are more likely than not to succeed and a remedy is possible in the upcoming election. The plaintiff must prove use by clear and convincing evidence. Nothing requires cancelling, editing or labelling content where inconsistent with federal law. Takes effect immediately.
